key_insight: HyperTool reframes tool use for LLM agents by hiding repetitive low-level execution details and exposing a more compact, executable interface. This reduces context waste and lets the model focus on higher-level decisions instead of step-by-step data plumbing.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the "execution-granularity mismatch" in tool-augmented agents, where locally deterministic tool workflows are broken into many model-visible atomic calls. That leads to bloated reasoning traces, unnecessary context usage, and fragile handling of intermediate values.
method: Introduces HyperTool, a unified executable MCP-style tool interface for agent workflows.
Consolidates step-wise tool invocations, observations, and value transfers into a more abstract execution layer.
Reduces the amount of low-level reasoning the model must explicitly manage in the visible trace.
impact: For practitioners, this can make tool-augmented agents more efficient, easier to scale, and less context-intensive. It may also improve reliability by separating high-level planning from deterministic tool execution.

paper_authors: Yaxin Du, Yifan Zhou, Yujie Ge, Jiajun Wang, Xianghe Pang
